common_definitions: Apply the following fixed bearing policy to the CURRENT factual state; its eligible wheel and pedal form one native input. These are supplied engineering rules, not a claim that the input is optimal or pursuit-equivalent. Read x=ego_x_m and y=ego_y_m from the road.preview row whose ahead_m equals 15, using road.preview_columns. The 15 m centre bearing theta equals round(degrees(atan2(y,x)),4), calculated from those rounded raw coordinates. If road.preview_15m_bearing_deg is present, read theta directly from that factual scalar; otherwise compute theta yourself. Positive theta means LEFT of the kart nose, negative theta means RIGHT. Thresholds are -22, -7, +7 and +22 degrees; exact threshold ties choose the smaller absolute wheel angle. Let speed=kart.speed_m_s and L=current_road_frame.velocity_left_m_s. Let B be true exactly when road.on_road is false, OR (road.offset_m>0 AND road.left_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L>=0.5), OR (road.offset_m<0 AND road.right_edge_clearance_m<=3 AND L<=-0.5). Otherwise B is false. The speed<2 acceleration rule takes priority even when B is true.

wheel_facts.units: m,s; display angles deg, handling angles rad. Positive steering/yaw/curvature/ego y/offset are LEFT; ego x forward. Wheel angle is actual; control is held input. road_vs_kart=road tangent minus kart heading. road_turn=future tangent minus current ROAD tangent. Preview distances are centreline arc from nearest projection. Edge clearance<0 is outside. Need=v²×|curvature|; grip ratio>1 exceeds current surface grip. Grip radius excludes steering limits/transients.
